headline: Persistent Bathroom Moisture and Foggy Mirrors: How to Select an Exhaust Fan Upgrade
articleBody:
Overview
Bathroom moisture that lingers on mirrors and walls isn't just an annoyance; it can slowly degrade drywall and trim. Upgrading your exhaust fan restores healthy airflow and protects your bathroom remodel investment.

Key Benefits
A properly sized unit removes humid air before it settles. Benefits include preventing mildew, protecting custom cabinetry, and meeting efficiency standards using quiet ENERGY STAR options. Intermittent fans require at least 50 CFM, while continuous models run near 20 to 25 CFM to manage background humidity.

Process Breakdown
We begin by inspecting your existing fan box, wiring, and exhaust pathway. Next, we determine the correct CFM based on room dimensions, route rigid ducting directly to the outside, seal joints against leaks, and test damper movement.

Real Examples
In older Salt Lake Valley bathrooms, we frequently find flexible ducts venting straight into attic insulation. Replacing them with smooth, insulated metal pipes vented through the roof immediately stops attic moisture accumulation.

What to Prepare Before You Start
Check whether you have exterior venting, note whether your walls show moisture stains, and consider adding automated humidity-sensing controls.
